Core API Reference: State, Components, & Lifecycle

This page details the foundational functions of Meld, exported from meld.core.js. Use the category filter chips below to show only specific modules of the runtime.

All
Reactivity
DOM & Templating
Lifecycle
Context / DI
dom since v1.0.0
defineMeld(tagName, setupFn)
→void

Registers a component as a native Custom Element (Web Component) in the global custom registry.

Parameters
NameTypeDescription
tagNamestringThe kebab-case name for the custom element (must contain a hyphen, e.g. my-counter).
setupFnFunctionThe setup function execution logic. Receives (element, { emit, inject }). Returns the template literal fragment or element representation.
Example
defineMeld('user-card', (el, { emit }) => {
  return meldHtml`
    

      
    

  `;
});
onMount onDestroy
reactivity since v1.0.0
meldState(initialObject)
→Proxy

Creates the core reactive state object. Any mutations made to properties on the returned Proxy will automatically trigger updates to affected DOM nodes.

Parameters
NameTypeDescription
initialObjectObjectA plain JavaScript object containing the properties that should be made reactive.
Returns

A deep Proxy wrapping the initial object, enabling granular dependency tracking and reactivity.

Example
const state = meldState({ count: 0, theme: 'dark' });

// Mutating state triggers reactives updates
state.count++;

computed
reactivity since v1.0.0
computed(getterFn)
→ReadonlySignal

Creates a derived, cached, read-only value. The getter only recalculates if the reactive signals accessed within it undergo changes.

Parameters
NameTypeDescription
getterFnFunctionA function returning the computed value. Any reactive state properties accessed during execution are tracked.
Example
const state = meldState({ firstName: 'Ada', lastName: 'Lovelace' });
const fullName = computed(() => `${state.firstName} ${state.lastName}`);

// Accessing fullName caches the result
console.log(fullName.value); // "Ada Lovelace"

meldState
lifecycle since v1.0.0
onMount(fn)
→void

Registers a lifecycle hook that executes immediately after the current component custom element is connected to the DOM.

Parameters
NameTypeDescription
fnFunctionCallback logic containing setup steps (e.g., event listeners, timers).
Example
defineMeld('timer-widget', () => {
  onMount(() => {
    console.log('Timer element connected!');
  });
});
onDestroy
lifecycle since v1.0.0
onDestroy(fn)
→void

Registers a lifecycle hook that executes immediately after the current component is disconnected from the DOM. Use to release resources and prevent memory leaks.

Parameters
NameTypeDescription
fnFunctionCallback containing cleanup logic (e.g., clearing intervals, removing global events).
onMount
context since v1.1.0
provide(key, value)
→void

Shares a dependency value down the component tree. Any descendant component can retrieve this value via inject using the matching key.

Parameters
NameTypeDescription
keystring | SymbolIdentifier for the dependency.
valueanyThe value or reactive state to distribute.
Example
defineMeld('theme-provider', () => {
  const config = meldState({ theme: 'blue' });
  provide('theme-config', config);
});
inject
context since v1.1.0
inject(key, defaultValue?)
→any

Injects a dependency provided by an ancestor component. If the key is not found, the optional default value is returned.

Parameters
NameTypeDescription
keystring | SymbolIdentifier of the provided value.
defaultValue?anyFallback value if the provider was not found up the tree.
Example
defineMeld('themed-button', (el, { inject }) => {
  const theme = inject('theme-config', { theme: 'gray' });
  return meldHtml``;
});
